# Physical and Environmental Protection Standard

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes requirements for physical and environmental protection of information systems and facilities at Acme Health. This standard applies to all facilities housing systems that process, store, or transmit electronic protected health information (ePHI) and other sensitive organizational data.

## 2. Policy and Procedures

### 2.1 Policy Development

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate to applicable personnel or roles a physical and environmental protection policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 PE-1 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-1 High | ARC-AMPE PE-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the physical and environmental protection policy and the associated physical and environmental protection controls. [NIST 800-53 PE-1 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-1 High | ARC-AMPE PE-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.2 Roles and Responsibilities

Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the physical and environmental protection policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 PE-1 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-1 High | ARC-AMPE PE-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.3 Policy and Procedure Review

Acme Health must review and update the physical and environmental protection policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 PE-1 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-1 High]

Acme Health must review and update the physical and environmental protection policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE PE-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must review and update the physical and environmental protection procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 PE-1 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-1 High]

Acme Health must review and update the physical and environmental protection procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE PE-1 AE Mandatory]

## 3. Documentation Requirements

### 3.1 Documentation Maintenance

Acme Health must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)]

Acme Health must maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by this subpart to be documented. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)]

### 3.2 Documentation Retention

Acme Health must retain the documentation required by paragraph (b)(1) of this section for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)]

### 3.3 Documentation Access and Review

Acme Health must make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 4. Facility Access Control

### 4.1 General Requirements

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to its electronic information systems and the facility or facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring that properly authorized access is allowed. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(a)(1)]

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(a)(2)(ii)]

### 4.2 Facility Access Procedures

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(a)(2)(i)]

Acme Health must implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software programs for testing and revision. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(a)(2)(iii)]

### 4.3 Facility Maintenance Documentation

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility which are related to security (for example, hardware, walls, doors, and locks). [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(a)(2)(iv)]

## 5. Physical Access Authorization

### 5.1 Authorized Access List

Acme Health must develop, approve, and maintain a list of individuals with authorized access to the facility where the system resides. [NIST 800-53 PE-2 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-2 High | ARC-AMPE PE-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must issue authorization credentials for facility access. [NIST 800-53 PE-2 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-2 High | ARC-AMPE PE-2 AE Mandatory]

### 5.2 Access List Review

Acme Health must review the access list detailing authorized facility access by individuals [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 PE-2 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-2 High]

Acme Health must review the access list detailing authorized facility access by individuals at least every six (6) months. [ARC-AMPE PE-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must remove individuals from the facility access list when access is no longer required. [NIST 800-53 PE-2 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-2 High | ARC-AMPE PE-2 AE Mandatory]

### 5.3 Authorization Criteria

Acme Health must authorize physical access to the facility where the system resides based on position or role. [NIST 800-53 PE-2(1)]

Acme Health must restrict unescorted access to the facility where the system resides to personnel with [Selection (one or more): security clearances for all information contained within the system; formal access authorizations for all information contained within the system; need for access to all information contained within the system; [Assignment: organization-defined physical access authorizations]]. [NIST 800-53 PE-2(3)]

### 5.4 Visitor Identification

Acme Health must require two forms of identification from the following forms of identification for visitor access to the facility where the system resides: [Assignment: organization-defined list of acceptable forms of identification]. [NIST 800-53 PE-2(2)]

## 6. Physical Access Control Systems

### 6.1 Access Control Enforcement

Acme Health must enforce physical access authorizations at [Assignment: organization-defined entry and exit points] by verifying individual access authorizations before granting access to the facility and controlling ingress and egress to the facility using [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined systems or devices]; guards]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must enforce physical access authorizations at entry and exit points to the facility where the system resides by verifying individual access authorizations before granting access to the facility and controlling ingress and egress to the facility using organization-defined physical access control systems or devices and/or guards. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

### 6.2 Physical Access Audit Logs

Acme Health must maintain physical access audit logs for [Assignment: organization-defined entry or exit points]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must maintain physical access audit logs for entry or exit points. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

### 6.3 Public Access Areas

Acme Health must control access to areas within the facility designated as publicly accessible by implementing the following controls: [Assignment: organization-defined physical access controls]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must control access to areas within the facility designated as publicly accessible by implementing organization-defined security safeguards or physical access controls. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

### 6.4 Visitor Escort and Control

Acme Health must escort visitors and control visitor activity [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must escort visitors and control visitor activity in organization-defined circumstances requiring visitor escorts and control of visitor activity. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

### 6.5 Physical Access Device Management

Acme Health must secure keys, combinations, and other physical access devices. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High | ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must inventory [Assignment: organization-defined physical access devices] every [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must inventory organization-defined physical access devices every ninety (90) days. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must change combinations and keys [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and/or when keys are lost, combinations are compromised, or when individuals possessing the keys or combinations are transferred or terminated. [NIST 800-53 PE-3 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-3 High]

Acme Health must change combinations and keys at least every one (1) year or earlier as required by a security-relevant event and/or when keys are lost, combinations are compromised, or when individuals possessing the keys or combinations are transferred or terminated. [ARC-AMPE PE-3 AE Mandatory]

### 6.6 Additional Physical Access Controls

Acme Health must enforce physical access authorizations to the system in addition to the physical access controls for the facility at [Assignment: organization-defined physical spaces]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(1) High]

Acme Health must perform security checks [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] at the physical perimeter of the facility or system for exfiltration of information or removal of system components. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(2)]

Acme Health must employ guards to control [Assignment: organization-defined physical access points] to the facility where the system resides 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(3)]

Acme Health must use lockable physical casings to protect [Assignment: organization-defined system components] from unauthorized physical access. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(4)]

Acme Health must employ [Assignment: organization-defined anti-tamper technologies] to [Selection (one or more): detect; prevent] physical tampering or alteration of [Assignment: organization-defined hardware components] within the system. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(5)]

Acme Health must limit access using physical barriers. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(7)]

Acme Health must employ access control vestibules at [Assignment: organization-defined locations]. [NIST 800-53 PE-3(8)]

## 7. Workstation Physical Security

Acme Health must implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information, to restrict access to authorized users. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(c)]

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(b)]

## 8. Access Control for Transmission Media

### 8.1 Distribution and Transmission Lines

Acme Health must control physical access to [Assignment: organization-defined system distribution and transmission lines] within organizational facilities using [Assignment: organization-defined security controls]. [NIST 800-53 PE-4 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-4 High]

Acme Health must control physical access to organization-defined system distribution and transmission lines within organizational facilities using organization-defined security controls or safeguards. [ARC-AMPE PE-4 AE Mandatory]

### 8.2 Physical Port Management

Acme Health must disable any physical ports (e.g., wiring closets and patch panels) not in use. [ARC-AMPE PE-4 AE Mandatory]

## 9. Access Control for Output Devices

Acme Health must control physical access to output from [Assignment: organization-defined output devices] to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining the output. [NIST 800-53 PE-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-5 High]

Acme Health must control physical access to output from organization-defined output devices to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining the output. [ARC-AMPE PE-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must link individual identity to receipt of output from output devices. [NIST 800-53 PE-5(2)]

## 10. Monitoring Physical Access

### 10.1 Physical Access Monitoring Requirements

Acme Health must monitor physical access to the facility where the system resides to detect and respond to physical security incidents. [NIST 800-53 PE-6 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-6 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-6 High | ARC-AMPE PE-6 AE Mandatory]

### 10.2 Physical Access Log Review

Acme Health must review physical access logs [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and upon occurrence of [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 PE-6 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-6 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-6 High]

Acme Health must review physical access logs at least monthly (every thirty [30] days) and upon occurrence of organization-defined events or potential indications of events. [ARC-AMPE PE-6 AE Mandatory]

### 10.3 Incident Coordination

Acme Health must coordinate results of reviews and investigations with the organizational incident response capability. [NIST 800-53 PE-6 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-6 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-6 High | ARC-AMPE PE-6 AE Mandatory]

### 10.4 Intrusion Detection Systems

Acme Health must monitor physical access to the facility where the system resides using physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment. [NIST 800-53 PE-6(1) Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-6(1) High | ARC-AMPE PE-6(1) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must recognize [Assignment: organization-defined classes or types of intrusions] and initiate [Assignment: organization-defined response actions] using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 PE-6(2)]

### 10.5 Video Surveillance

Acme Health must employ video surveillance of [Assignment: organization-defined operational areas]; review video recordings [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and retain video recordings for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 PE-6(3)]

### 10.6 Additional Monitoring

Acme Health must monitor physical access to the system in addition to the physical access monitoring of the facility at [Assignment: organization-defined physical spaces]. [NIST 800-53 PE-6(4) High]

## 11. Visitor Control

### 11.1 Visitor Access Records

Acme Health must maintain visitor access records to the facility where the system resides for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 PE-8 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-8 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-8 High]

Acme Health must maintain visitor access records to the facility where the system resides for at least one (1) year. [ARC-AMPE PE-8 AE Mandatory]

### 11.2 Visitor Record Review

Acme Health must review visitor access records [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 PE-8 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-8 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-8 High]

Acme Health must review visitor access records at least monthly (every thirty [30] days). [ARC-AMPE PE-8 AE Mandatory]

### 11.3 Anomaly Reporting

Acme Health must report anomalies in visitor access records to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel]. [NIST 800-53 PE-8 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-8 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-8 High]

Acme Health must report anomalies in visitor access records to organization-defined personnel or roles. [ARC-AMPE PE-8 AE Mandatory]

### 11.4 Visitor Record Content

Visitor access records must include at a minimum: name and organization of the person visiting; visitor's signature; form of identification; date of access; time of entry and departure; purpose of visit; and name and organization of person visited. [ARC-AMPE PE-8 AE Mandatory]

### 11.5 Automated Visitor Management

Acme Health must maintain and review visitor access records using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 PE-8(1) High]

### 11.6 Privacy Protection

Acme Health must limit personally identifiable information contained in visitor access records to the following elements identified in the privacy risk assessment: [Assignment: organization-defined elements]. [NIST 800-53 PE-8(3)]

## 12. Power Equipment and Cabling

### 12.1 Power Equipment Protection

Acme Health must protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction. [NIST 800-53 PE-9 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-9 High | ARC-AMPE PE-9 AE Mandatory]

### 12.2 Infrastructure Maintenance Access

Acme Health must only permit authorized maintenance personnel to access infrastructure assets, including power generators; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems; cabling; and wiring closets. [ARC-AMPE PE-9 AE Mandatory]

### 12.3 Power Cabling Redundancy

Acme Health must employ redundant power cabling paths that are physically separated by [Assignment: organization-defined distance]. [NIST 800-53 PE-9(1)]

### 12.4 Voltage Controls

Acme Health must employ automatic voltage controls for [Assignment: organization-defined critical system components]. [NIST 800-53 PE-9(2)]

## 13. Emergency Shutoff

### 13.1 Emergency Power Shutoff Capability

Acme Health must provide the capability of shutting off power to [Assignment: organization-defined system or individual system components] in emergency situations. [NIST 800-53 PE-10 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-10 High]

Acme Health must provide the capability of shutting off power to an organization-defined system or individual system components in emergency situations. [ARC-AMPE PE-10 AE Mandatory]

### 13.2 Emergency Shutoff Switch Placement

Acme Health must place emergency shutoff switches or devices in [Assignment: organization-defined location] to facilitate access for authorized personnel. [NIST 800-53 PE-10 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-10 High]

Acme Health must place emergency shutoff switches or devices in an organization-defined location by system or system component to facilitate access for authorized personnel. [ARC-AMPE PE-10 AE Mandatory]

### 13.3 Emergency Shutoff Protection

Acme Health must protect emergency power shutoff capability from unauthorized activation. [NIST 800-53 PE-10 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-10 High | ARC-AMPE PE-10 AE Mandatory]

### 13.4 Main Power Switch Requirements

Acme Health must implement and maintain a main power switch or emergency cut-off switch, prominently marked and protected by a cover, for data centers, servers, and mainframe rooms. [ARC-AMPE PE-10 AE Mandatory]

## 14. Emergency Power

### 14.1 Uninterruptible Power Supply

Acme Health must provide an uninterruptible power supply to facilitate [Selection: an orderly shutdown of the system; transition of the system to long-term alternate power] in the event of a primary power source loss. [NIST 800-53 PE-11 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-11 High]

Acme Health must provide an uninterruptible power supply to facilitate an orderly shutdown of the system and/or transition of the system to long-term alternate power in the event of a primary power source loss. [ARC-AMPE PE-11 AE Mandatory]

### 14.2 Emergency Power Testing

Acme Health must test emergency power equipment on a schedule that complies with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, with testing performed no less often than every three (3) years. [ARC-AMPE PE-11 AE Mandatory]

### 14.3 Long-Term Alternate Power

Acme Health must provide an alternate power supply for the system that is activated [Selection: manually; automatically] and that can maintain minimally required operational capability in the event of an extended loss of the primary power source. [NIST 800-53 PE-11(1) High]

### 14.4 Self-Contained Power Supply

Acme Health must provide an alternate power supply for the system that is self-contained, not reliant on external power generation, and capable of maintaining [Selection: minimally required operational capability; full operational capability] in the event of an extended loss of the primary power source. [NIST 800-53 PE-11(2)]

## 15. Emergency Lighting

### 15.1 Automatic Emergency Lighting

Acme Health must employ and maintain automatic emergency lighting for the system that activates in the event of a power outage or disruption and that covers emergency exits and evacuation routes within the facility. [NIST 800-53 PE-12 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-12 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-12 High | ARC-AMPE PE-12 AE Mandatory]

### 15.2 Emergency Lighting Testing

Acme Health must test emergency lighting equipment on a schedule that complies with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, with testing performed no less often than every three (3) years. [ARC-AMPE PE-12 AE Mandatory]

### 15.3 Essential Areas Coverage

Acme Health must provide emergency lighting for all areas within the facility supporting essential mission and business functions. [NIST 800-53 PE-12(1)]

## 16. Fire Protection

### 16.1 Fire Detection and Suppression Systems

Acme Health must employ and maintain fire detection and suppression systems that are supported by an independent energy source. [NIST 800-53 PE-13 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-13 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-13 High | ARC-AMPE PE-13 AE Mandatory]

### 16.2 Fire Protection Testing

Acme Health must test fire protection equipment on a schedule that complies with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, with testing performed no less often than every three (3) years. [ARC-AMPE PE-13 AE Mandatory]

### 16.3 Automatic Fire Detection

Acme Health must employ fire detection systems that activate automatically and notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] and [Assignment: organization-defined emergency responders] in the event of a fire. [NIST 800-53 PE-13(1) Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-13(1) High]

Acme Health must employ fire detection systems that activate automatically and notify organization-defined personnel or roles and defined emergency responders in the event of a fire. [ARC-AMPE PE-13(1) AE Mandatory]

### 16.4 Automatic Fire Suppression

Acme Health must employ fire suppression systems that activate automatically and notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] and [Assignment: organization-defined emergency responders], and employ an automatic fire suppression capability when the facility is not staffed on a continuous basis. [NIST 800-53 PE-13(2) High]

### 16.5 Fire Protection Inspections

Acme Health must ensure that the facility undergoes [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] fire protection inspections by authorized and qualified inspectors and identified deficiencies are resolved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 PE-13(4)]

## 17. Environmental Controls

### 17.1 Temperature and Humidity Control

Acme Health must maintain [Selection (one or more): temperature; humidity; pressure; radiation; [Assignment: organization-defined environmental control]] levels within the facility where the system resides at [Assignment: organization-defined acceptable levels]. [NIST 800-53 PE-14 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-14 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-14 High]

Acme Health must maintain temperature, humidity, and pressure levels at acceptable vendor-specified levels within the facility where the system resides. [ARC-AMPE PE-14 AE Mandatory]

### 17.2 Environmental Monitoring

Acme Health must monitor environmental control levels [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 PE-14 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-14 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-14 High]

Acme Health must monitor environmental control levels within the defined frequency. [ARC-AMPE PE-14 AE Mandatory]

### 17.3 ASHRAE Compliance

Acceptable vendor-specified levels should be consistent with American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) document, Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments. [ARC-AMPE PE-14 AE Mandatory]

### 17.4 Automatic Environmental Controls

Acme Health must employ the following automatic environmental controls in the facility to prevent fluctuations potentially harmful to the system: [Assignment: organization-defined automatic environmental controls]. [NIST 800-53 PE-14(1)]

### 17.5 Environmental Control Monitoring Alerts

Acme Health must employ environmental control monitoring that provides an alarm or notification of changes potentially harmful to personnel or equipment to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 PE-14(2)]

## 18. Water Damage Protection

### 18.1 Master Shutoff Valves

Acme Health must protect the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel. [NIST 800-53 PE-15 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-15 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-15 High | ARC-AMPE PE-15 AE Mandatory]

### 18.2 Water Damage Protection Testing

Acme Health must test water damage protection equipment on a schedule that complies with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, with testing performed no less often than every three (3) years. [ARC-AMPE PE-15 AE Mandatory]

### 18.3 Water Detection Systems

Acme Health must detect the presence of water near the system and alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 PE-15(1) High]

## 19. Delivery and Removal

### 19.1 System Component Control

Acme Health must authorize and control [Assignment: organization-defined types of system components] entering and exiting the facility. [NIST 800-53 PE-16 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-16 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-16 High]

Acme Health must authorize and control all system components entering and exiting the facility. [ARC-AMPE PE-16 AE Mandatory]

### 19.2 Component Movement Records

Acme Health must maintain records of the system components entering and exiting the facility. [NIST 800-53 PE-16 Low | NIST 800-53 PE-16 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-16 High | ARC-AMPE PE-16 AE Mandatory]

### 19.3 Device and Media Controls

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media that contain electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(1)]

### 19.4 Media Disposition

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic protected health information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(i)]

Acme Health must implement procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(ii)]

### 19.5 Accountability

Acme Health must maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(iii)]

### 19.6 Data Backup and Storage

Acme Health must create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information, when needed, before movement of equipment. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(iv)]

## 20. Alternate Work Sites

### 20.1 Alternate Work Site Designation

Acme Health must determine and document the [Assignment: organization-defined alternate work sites] allowed for use by employees. [NIST 800-53 PE-17 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-17 High]

Acme Health must determine and document the alternate work sites allowed for use by employees. [ARC-AMPE PE-17 AE Mandatory]

### 20.2 Alternate Work Site Controls

Acme Health must employ the following controls at alternate work sites: [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST 800-53 PE-17 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-17 High]

Acme Health must employ the following controls at alternate work sites: organization-defined controls. [ARC-AMPE PE-17 AE Mandatory]

### 20.3 Control Effectiveness Assessment

Acme Health must assess the effectiveness of controls at alternate work sites. [NIST 800-53 PE-17 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-17 High | ARC-AMPE PE-17 AE Mandatory]

### 20.4 Incident Communication

Acme Health must provide a means for employees to communicate with information security and privacy personnel in case of incidents. [NIST 800-53 PE-17 Moderate | NIST 800-53 PE-17 High | ARC-AMPE PE-17 AE Mandatory]

## 21. Location of System Components

Acme Health must position system components within the facility to minimize potential damage from [Assignment: organization-defined physical and environmental hazards] and to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access. [NIST 800-53 PE-18 High]

---

**Document Control:**
- **Owner:** [Assignment: organization-defined official]
- **Review Frequency:** At least annually or following organization-defined events
- **Retention Period:** 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later
